quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a road where traffic moves in both directions.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have their seat belts on.
Make sure only adults have their seat belts on.
Make sure only children have their seat belts on.
Make sure everyone in the car has their seat belt on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has their seat belt on.
questions.explanation: Get in the habit of fastening your seat belt every time you enter your car. Before you start the engine, check that you and all passengers have buckled up.

questions.question: When you pass an emergency vehicle parked on the right side of the road, you should:

options.text: Move to another lane or slow down.
Ask the emergency worker if they need help.
Move closer to the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane or slow down.
questions.explanation: When passing a stopped emergency vehicle on the right side, you must change lanes away from it if you can do so safely. If you cannot change lanes safely, you must slow down.

questions.question: Before you move back to your original lane after passing another car, you should:

options.text: See both headlights of the car you passed in your mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the car you passed in your mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing is allowed, watch your rearview mirror until you can see both headlights of the car you passed. This means you have enough space to safely return to your original lane.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is helping them cross the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must always have the right-of-way, regardless of other conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that turning right is not allowed at this location.

questions.question: When must drivers let pedestrians in a crosswalk go first?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave at you first.
Only if the pedestrians are not using their phones.

questions.explanation: Always stop completely at a crosswalk to let pedestrians and other vehicles go first. You can only move forward after your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: Fatigue makes it more likely that you will:

options.text: Fall asleep while driving and crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fall asleep while driving and crash.
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows your reaction time, affects your judgment about speed and distance, and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. This puts you and others at serious risk of injury or death.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle when you encounter:

options.text: A stop sign at an intersection.
A traffic officer ordering you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer signals you to stop.

questions.question: Which of these is a common cause of traffic accidents?

options.text: Following too closely behind other vehicles

questions.explanation: Speeding causes many crashes. Not paying attention can lead to collisions with other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a traffic law sign. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: How should you change from one lane to another?

options.text: When a car is in your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully. Only change lanes when needed. Each lane change increases your risk of an accident.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol from your system. Nothing else, like eating or drinking, can speed up this process.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Never pass if you cannot see clearly, if there is oncoming traffic, at an intersection, near a railroad crossing, on a bridge, or when a school bus has red flashing lights on.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain activity and reduces your driving skills. It makes your reaction time slower and your judgment worse.

questions.question: A driver should watch:

options.text: Directly in front of their car only.
Only the middle of the road.
Beside, ahead, and behind their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beside, ahead, and behind their car.
questions.explanation: Good drivers watch all around their vehicle. You need to know what is happening on all sides and behind you.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to turn.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Continue driving and use the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn to catch your exit. Go to the next exit instead.

questions.question: What can reduce road rage?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws and signs. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: In Oklahoma, all motor vehicles must have liability insurance.
questions.explanation: Oklahoma law requires all vehicle owners and drivers to have liability insurance. Every vehicle must be insured, even if you do not own it.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Do not worry about how many tracks to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop if a train is coming.
